In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both endocardial (and epicardial) synchrony are important and that the two are nearly always achieved together.
both endo-epicardial synchrony is important for cardiac resynchronization therapy.
electrical synchrony, as defined by fusion of native with paced activation, is not required for effective mechanical synchrony, as measured by LV pressure-volume loop analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
electrical synchrony is not a necessary prerequisite for mechanical synchrony, but that the degree of electrical synchrony is a good indicator for the degree of mechanical synchrony.
endocardial and/or epicardial electrical mapping is sufficient for assessing the need for LV pacing in patients.

the electrical delay measured on the epicardial surface of the heart during cardiac resynchronization is a good estimate of the electrical delay of inner wall layers as long as the electrical delay on the epicardia is measured during the same cardiac cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the epicardial surface is a reasonable surrogate for the endocardium when assessing the timing of electrical activation during cardiac resynchronization.
endocardial and/or epicardial electrical mapping is equally useful to assess electrical synchrony.
